statement:

An empty string or single character is considered a valid palindrome.
constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters.

editorial.approach: Clean the string to retain only lowercase alphanumeric characters, then check if it equals its reverse. Or use two pointers, skipping non-alphanumeric elements.

hints: You can strip non-alphanumeric characters using a regex like `/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g`.
Alternatively, use a two-pointer approach starting at the extremes.
Skip indices where `s[left]` or `s[right]` is not alphanumeric, then compare lowercase values.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Remove all non-alphanumeric characters, convert the string to lowercase, and check if it reads the same backwards.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use two pointers, checking characters from both ends. Skip any non-alphanumeric characters on-the-fly, avoiding any helper array or string allocations.

interviewExplanation: While stripping non-alphanumeric characters is clean, it allocates O(n) memory. An in-place two-pointer approach skips spaces and punctuation dynamically, checking matching letters in O(n) time and O(1) space.
